items.stem: Metals become dull when exposed to air. Why?
items.answer: Metals become dull when exposed to air due to the formation of a thin layer of oxide, carbonate or sulphide on their surfaces.
items.ocr: Printed question number was lost by MinerU - the text runs straight on from the 'ONE MARK QUESTIONS' heading. Numbered 1 from position, since the next printed number is 2.

items.stem: What length of wire can be drawn from one gram of gold?
items.answer: Two kilometres long wire can be drawn from one gram of gold.
items.ocr: OCR read 'can he drawn'; repaired to 'can be drawn'.

items.stem: What is meant by thermal conductivity of metals?
items.answer: Conductivity of heat in metals is known as thermal conductivity.

items.stem: Name the poorest conductors of heat among metals.
items.answer: Lead is the poorest conductor of heat among metals.

items.stem: Arrange the following in decreasing order of their electrical conductivity: Mercury, Copper, Tungsten, Aluminium.
items.answer: Copper, Aluminium, Tungsten and Mercury.

items.stem: Explain the statement, “metals are sonorous”.
items.answer: This means that metals produce a sound when struck by an object.

items.stem: Name a metal which offers higher resistance to the passage of electricity than copper.
items.answer: Mercury offers higher resistance to the passage of electricity than copper.
items.ocr: Printed question number dropped by MinerU; numbered 7 from position (between printed 6 and 8).

items.stem: Name two metals both of which are very ductile as well as very malleable.
items.answer: Gold and silver.

items.stem: Name some non-metals which are solid at room temperature.
items.answer: Carbon, sulphur, phosphorus, iodine, etc.

items.stem: Name the non-metal which is used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils to make vegetable ghee.
items.answer: Hydrogen.

items.stem: Name the most abundant element in the earth’s crust.
items.answer: Oxygen.

items.stem: Name the second most abundant element in the earth’s crust.
items.answer: Silicon.

items.stem: Name two metals which have very low melting point.
items.answer: Gallium and caesium have very low melting point.

items.stem: Name two most malleable metals.
items.answer: Gold and silver are the most malleable metals.

items.stem: Name one metal and one non-metal which exists in liquid state at room temperature.
items.answer: Metal - Mercury; Non-metal - Bromine.

items.stem: A non-metal X exists in two different forms Y and Z. Y is the hardest natural substance, whereas Z is a good conductor of electricity. Identify X, Y and Z.
items.answer: X is carbon, Y is diamond and Z is graphite.
items.ocr: LaTeX italic markers ($X$, $\textit{Z. Y}$) stripped back to plain letters.

items.stem: What is the general nature of metal oxides?
items.answer: The metal oxides are generally basic in nature.
items.ocr: Source tag printed as 'Dehi 2017'; read as Delhi 2017.

items.stem: What are alkalis? Give one example of alkalis.
items.answer: Those bases which are soluble in water are called alkalis. Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is an example of an alkali.

items.stem: Name two amphoteric oxides.
items.answer: Aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃) and zinc oxide (ZnO).
items.ocr: OCR mangled the formula to 'Al O $^3$'; restored to Al₂O₃.

items.stem: What happens when magnesium is heated to its ignition temperature?
items.answer: It burns with blinding white light to form magnesium oxide.
items.ocr: A stray 'b' was printed after 'Ans'; the answer read 'white ight' and was repaired to 'white light'.

items.stem: What happens when iron is heated to a high temperature?
items.answer: Iron does not burn on heating but glows brightly.

items.stem: What happens when copper is heated to a very high temperature?
items.answer: Copper does not burn, but the hot metal is coated with a layer of black substance known as copper(II) oxide.

items.stem: Name two metals which do not react with air even at high temperature.
items.answer: Silver and gold do not react with air even at high temperature.

items.stem: What happens when metals react with water?
items.answer: Metals react with water to form metal oxides or metal hydroxides and hydrogen gas.

items.stem: Name two metals that react violently with cold water.
items.answer: Potassium and sodium react violently with cold water.

items.stem: Name the metal which does not react with dilute acids.
items.answer: Copper does not react with dilute acids.

items.stem: Write the chemical equation for the reaction taking place when a piece of calcium metal is placed in water.
items.answer: Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂
items.ocr: LaTeX $\mathrm{Ca}+2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow ...$ rewritten to Unicode with the → arrow.

items.stem: Write the chemical equation for the reaction taking place when steam is passed over red hot iron.
items.answer: 3Fe(s) + 4H₂O(g) → Fe₃O₄(s) + 4H₂(g)
items.ocr: Question number dropped by MinerU; numbered 28 from position (between printed 27 and 30, with 29 also unnumbered). items.stem: Give reason for the following: Na, K and Ca metals form hydrides by combining with hydrogen gas, but most other metals do not.
items.answer: This is because Na, K and Ca are highly electropositive in nature.
items.ocr: Question number dropped by MinerU; numbered 29 from position (it sits between item 28 and printed 30). A stray '$\therefore$' artefact stood where the colon is printed.

items.stem: An element M on reacting with oxygen forms an oxide M₂O. This oxide dissolves in water and turns red litmus blue. State whether the element M is a metal or a non-metal.
items.answer: M is a metal since metal oxides are generally basic in nature.
items.ocr: Formula printed as 'M $2$ O'; rewritten as M₂O.

items.stem: A metal X on heating in air does not burn, but acquires a black coating of the substance Y on its surface. Name the metal X and the substance Y.
items.answer: Metal X is copper and the substance Y is copper(II) oxide.

items.stem: In nature, metal P is found in the form of its compounds and metal Q is found in the free state. Which of the two will be nearer to the top of the activity series of metals?
items.answer: Metal P.

items.stem: An element A forms two oxides AO and AO₂. The oxide AO is neutral whereas the oxide AO₂ is acidic in nature. Would you call element A a metal or a non-metal?
items.answer: Element A is a non-metal, as only non-metals form neutral and acidic oxides.
items.ocr: Page furniture '41. NODIA' (a watermark plus the displaced number of a later question) was printed inside this question and has been stripped.

items.stem: Name the compounds formed by metals when they react with hydrogen.
items.answer: Hydrides.

items.stem: If copper metal is heated over a flame, it develops a coating. What is the colour and composition of this coating?
items.answer: A black colour coat is developed on the copper metal due to formation of CuO or copper oxide.

items.stem: Write the chemical equation for the reaction taking place when a piece of zinc is placed in a solution of copper(II) sulphate.
items.answer: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu
items.ocr: MinerU printed the reaction arrow as a bare '$' artefact; restored to → and subscripts applied.

items.stem: If P, Q, R, S, T represent metals in the decreasing order of their reactivity, which one of them is most likely to occur in the free state in nature?
items.answer: Metal T.

items.stem: Which one of the metals in the following group are (a) most reactive, (b) least reactive? Au, Na, Cu, Ca
items.answer: (a) Sodium (Na) is the most reactive in the above group. (b) Gold (Au) is the least reactive in the above group.
items.ocr: The metal list 'Au, Na, Cu, Ca' sits on the next page column and has been rejoined to the stem.

items.stem: Name one metal which reacts with very dilute HNO₃ to evolve hydrogen gas.
items.answer: Magnesium (Mg) / Manganese (Mn) reacts with very dilute HNO₃ to evolve H₂ gas.
items.ocr: 'HNO $_3$' and '$\mathrm{H}_2$' rewritten to HNO₃ and H₂.

items.stem: Why does copper not evolve hydrogen on reacting with dilute sulphuric acid?
items.answer: It happens so because copper is a less reactive metal; it occupies a place below hydrogen in the reactivity series.

items.stem: What are electrovalent compounds?
items.answer: The compounds formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal are known as ionic compounds or electrovalent compounds.
items.ocr: Question number missing from its place; the printed '41.' had been displaced up into the body of item 33 alongside the NODIA watermark. Numbered 41 from position.

items.stem: Show the ion formation in: (i) Sodium (ii) Chlorine
items.answer: (i) Sodium: Na (2,8,1) → Na⁺ (2,8) + e⁻   (ii) Chlorine: Cl (2,8,7) + e⁻ → Cl⁻ (2,8,8)

items.stem: What can you say about the solubility of electrovalent compounds?
items.answer: Electrovalent compounds are generally soluble in water and insoluble in solvents such as kerosene, petrol, etc.

items.stem: Write electronic configuration of an element having atomic number 11.
Write electronic configuration of an element having atomic number 13.
Ionic compounds are hard crystalline solids. Why?
items.answer: Ionic compounds are very hard solids due to strong force of attraction between positive and negative ions.

items.stem: Which metals are found in free state in nature?
items.answer: The metals at the bottom of the activity series are the least reactive. They are often found in a free state.

items.stem: Which metals are never found in free state in nature?
items.answer: The metals at the top of the activity series (K, Na, Ca, Mg and Al) are so reactive that they are never found in nature as free elements.
items.ocr: OCR inserted a stray full stop in 'activity .series'; removed.

items.stem: How are metals classified on the basis of reactivity?
items.answer: On the basis of reactivity, we can group the metals into the following three categories: (i) Metals of low reactivity; (ii) Metals of medium reactivity; (iii) Metals of high reactivity.

items.stem: Which metals are found as oxides, sulphides, etc. in the earth’s crust?
items.answer: The metals in the middle of the activity series (Zn, Fe, Pb, etc.) are moderately reactive. They are found in the earth’s crust mainly as oxides, sulphides or carbonates.

items.stem: Write the equation when manganese dioxide is heated with aluminium powder.
items.answer: 3MnO₂ + 4Al → 3Mn + 2Al₂O₃ + Heat
items.ocr: LaTeX $\mathrm{3MnO_2+4Al\longrightarrow ...}$ rewritten to Unicode subscripts with →.

items.stem: How are metals towards the top of the activity series extracted?
items.answer: They are extracted by electrolysis.

items.stem: In the refining of silver, the recovery of silver from silver nitrate solution involves displacement by copper metal. Give the reason for the same.
items.answer: Copper is more reactive than silver.

items.stem: What chemical process is used for obtaining a metal from its oxide?
items.answer: A metal is obtained from its oxide by the process of reduction.

items.stem: What is corrosion of metals?
items.answer: The eating away of upper layers of a metal due to the action of air and moisture is called corrosion.

items.stem: Which metals do not corrode easily?
items.answer: (i) Gold, (ii) Silver, (iii) Platinum.

items.stem: Name one metal which corrodes on being kept in atmosphere.
items.answer: Iron.

items.stem: Silver becomes blackish (tarnished) after some time. Why?
items.answer: A layer of silver sulphide (black in colour) is formed on the surface of silver-ware due to which it gets tarnished.

items.stem: Why does a greenish layer appear on a copper vessel if it is left for a few days in humid atmosphere without being cleaned? OR Copper articles become green when kept in moist air. Why? OR A green layer is generally formed on a copper plate left exposed to air for a week in a bathroom. What could this green substance be?
items.answer: The greenish layer on the copper articles (vessel or plate) is due to the coating of copper carbonate in moist air.
items.ocr: The bank prints three alternative wordings of the same question under one number, joined by 'or'; all three are kept in the stem.

items.stem: Give an advantage of corrosion of metals. OR Give an example to support that corrosion of some metals is an advantage.
items.answer: Corrosion of metals like iron, copper, silver, etc. is an advantage because it prevents the metal underneath from further damage.
items.ocr: Two alternative printed wordings kept, joined by OR.

items.stem: A vessel made of a metal M acquires a blackish tinge on exposure to air after a few days. Name the metal M and the black substance.
items.answer: The metal M is silver and the black substance is silver sulphide.

items.stem: Write one example of a metal having low melting point and a non-metal having high melting point.
items.answer: Low melting point metal - Gallium; high melting point non-metal - diamond.

items.stem: Write one example of a metal which is poor conductor of electricity and a non-metal which is good conductor of electricity.
items.answer: Metal which is poor conductor of electricity - [name lost in extraction; the standard answer is mercury, or lead]. Non-metal which is good conductor of electricity - Graphite.

items.stem: Explain the term Malleability.
items.answer: The property of metals by virtue of which they can be beaten into thin sheets is called malleability, e.g. gold and silver.

items.stem: Explain the term Ductility.
items.answer: The ability of metals to be drawn into thin wires is called ductility. Gold is the most ductile metal.

items.stem: Give one most suitable word for the following statement: (a) Metal oxides which show basic as well as acidic behaviour (b) Iodine, a non-metal, is shining.
items.answer: (a) Amphoteric oxide (b) Lustrous

items.stem: Give reason why electric wires are coated with plastic (PVC).
items.answer: The electric wires have a covering of PVC around them so that even if we happen to touch the current-carrying wire, the current will not pass through our body and hence we will not get an electric shock.

items.stem: Give reason: Generally no hydrogen gas is evolved when metals react with dilute nitric acid.
items.answer: Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises the hydrogen gas produced into water and itself gets reduced to any one of its oxides like NO, NO₂ or N₂O.

items.stem: Give reason: Ionic compounds are usually hard.
items.answer: They are solids and are somewhat hard because of the strong force of attraction between the positive and negative ions.
